source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They act only after a clot is fully formed and function mainly to dissolve the existing fibrin mesh","B":"They activate in a sequence that generates fibrin and helps stabilize the developing platelet plug","C":"They are identical to platelets and therefore have no separate role in secondary hemostasis","D":"They prevent platelet adhesion and keep fibrin from forming at the site of vascular injury"}}
source_row.rationale: Coagulation factors activate through coordinated pathways that culminate in thrombin generation and fibrin formation. Fibrin stabilizes the platelet plug and supports formation of a durable clot.
source_row.source_detail: Blood clotting process: clotting factors and fibrin stabilize the platelet plug; National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A nursing student asks how coagulation factors contribute to hemostasis after blood-vessel injury. Which response is correct?
